title: Stretch-In vs Glue-Down Carpet: Which Installation Is Right?
meta: Stretch-in carpet over pad is right for most Kirkland homes; glue-down wins on concrete, in home offices and big open rooms. Wills Flooring compares both.
keywords: stretch-in vs glue-down carpet, glue down carpet installation, tackless carpet installation, double glue carpet, carpet installation methods residential

blocks.lead: Stretch-in over a separate pad is the right installation for almost every Kirkland living room, bedroom and staircase; glue-down is the right choice on concrete slabs, in rooms with rolling chairs or wheelchairs, and in very large open spaces where a stretched carpet would eventually ripple.
blocks.detail: The two methods use different carpets, different pads and different repair paths, so the choice should be made before you pick a sample, not after.

blocks.html: When a Kirkland homeowner asks about carpet, the conversation is usually about color and softness. The installation method rarely comes up, yet it decides how the floor feels, how long it stays flat and what happens when a section gets damaged. A Houghton rambler with a plywood subfloor and a Totem Lake condo on a concrete slab should not get the same install. This post explains both methods, when each one wins and the questions to ask before the installer shows up.

items.title: Stretch-in (tackless)
items.text: Wood tack strips with angled pins are nailed around the perimeter. A separate pad is laid and stapled or glued down. The carpet is then power-stretched over the pad and hooked onto the pins. Nothing touches the carpet backing but air and pad.

items.title: Direct glue-down
items.text: The carpet is glued straight to the subfloor with no pad. The carpet usually has a dense attached cushion or a firm commercial backing. It cannot ripple, cannot shift and has a very low profile at doorways.

items.title: Double glue-down
items.text: A dense pad is glued to the subfloor, then the carpet is glued to the pad. You get the softness of a pad with the stability of glue. It is the method for big open rooms and for anyone who wants comfort plus a floor that never wrinkles.

items.title: Carpet tile
items.text: Modular squares set with a pressure-sensitive adhesive or peel-and-stick backing. Technically a glue-down. Good for a Bridle Trails home office or a kids' basement where a single spill should mean replacing one tile, not one room.

blocks.text: Which method for which Kirkland room

items.html: Living room and bedrooms in a Rose Hill or Finn Hill house: stretch-in over a quality pad. Plywood subfloor, normal room sizes, comfort matters most.
Staircase: stretch-in, either waterfall or Hollywood wrapped. Glue on stairs looks flat and fails at the nose.
Daylight basement on a slab: glue-down or double glue-down after a moisture test. Below-grade Kirkland slabs stay cool and damp, and a trapped pad is how basements start to smell.
Home office with a rolling chair: glue-down or carpet tile. Tech workers around Juanita and Houghton wear a bald spot into stretched carpet under the desk within two years.
Lakefront great room, 35 ft long: double glue-down. It keeps the softness clients want and stays flat through summer humidity swings off Lake Washington.
Totem Lake condo on a slab: glue-down with an acoustic pad, or stretch-in with a glued pad if the HOA sound rules allow. We check the building's requirement first.

a.title: Usually an installation shortcut
items: Knee-kicked instead of power-stretched, so it ripples in a year
Pad too thick or too soft for the carpet, which voids most carpet warranties
Tack strip too far from the wall, leaving a soft gap at the edge
Installed on a damp slab, trapping moisture under the pad

b.title: Usually a prep problem
items: Adhesive spread on a dusty or uneven slab and the carpet lifts at seams
No moisture test, and the glue lets go within a year
Wrong adhesive for the backing type
Subfloor imperfections telegraph through a thin carpet

blocks.title: Concrete needs a moisture test either way:
blocks.text: Kirkland basements and slab-on-grade condos regularly read higher than the carpet manufacturer allows. We test before recommending a method. If the slab is wet, the answer is not a different glue. It is fixing the moisture, or choosing a floor that tolerates it.
How to choose in five minutes

items.text: Plywood points to stretch-in. Concrete points to glue-down or a glued pad. If you are not sure, a heat register or a closet corner usually tells you.
Under about 30 ft in every direction, stretch-in is fine. Beyond that, plan on double glue-down or accept periodic re-stretching.
Office chairs, wheelchairs or a toddler's ride-on toy every day mean glue-down or carpet tile.

faq.q: Is glue-down carpet better than stretch-in?
faq.a: Neither is better everywhere. Stretch-in over a pad is softer, warmer and easier to replace, and suits most rooms with a wood subfloor. Glue-down is more stable, handles rolling chairs and concrete slabs, and never ripples. Match the method to the room rather than picking one for the whole house.

faq.q: Can you stretch-in carpet over concrete?
faq.a: Yes, but the pad has to be glued to the slab and the tack strip anchored with concrete nails or adhesive. The slab must test dry first, because a pad on a damp slab traps moisture. For many Kirkland basements a glue-down or double glue-down is the safer choice.

Direct glue-down has no separate pad, though many glue-down carpets have a thin attached cushion. Double glue-down adds a dense pad glued to the floor, then the carpet glued on top. That is how you get pad comfort in a room that needs glue-down stability.

faq.q: Why does my stretched carpet have ripples?
faq.a: Usually it was knee-kicked rather than power-stretched, or the pad was too thick for the carpet. Humidity swings and dragging heavy furniture make it worse. A re-stretch fixes it in an hour or two, and it is covered by the Wills Flooring 1-year workmanship warranty when we installed the carpet.

faq.q: Which method is better for a home office chair?
faq.a: Glue-down or carpet tile. A rolling chair pushes stretched carpet back and forth over the pad thousands of times, and a wrinkle or a worn spot follows. A glued carpet cannot move. If you want a stretched carpet anyway, use a hard chair mat under the desk.

faq.q: Is glue-down carpet hard to remove later?
faq.a: Harder than stretch-in. The carpet is cut into strips and pulled, then the adhesive residue is scraped or ground off before a new floor goes down. It adds time and cost to the next project. If you expect to change the floor within a few years, stretch-in is the easier path.
